claims.statement: Under a targeted internal intervention during decoding, Evo2-7B generates DNA whose encoded protein has a mean α-helix fraction significantly higher than the unintervened baseline, with a monotone dose-response.
claims.origin: task.md behavior (given) — helix-gain predicate of the bundled success criterion

data.source: Evo2-7B generations (baseline + steered) scored via ESMFold→DSSP; high/low-helix contrast set back-translated from labeled-SS proteins for CAA vector construction
data.used_n: realized: 1500 baseline gens (M1) + 13,500 steered gens (M3: 3 sites × 6 coefs × 3 seeds × 250) + 3,000 M4 controls (4 conditions × 750)
data.subset_note: DEV/TEST split enforced (vector built on DEV, C1/C2 tested on TEST)

claims.method: Committed: Steering Vectors / contrastive activation addition (CAA) at probe-selected residual site 28, coefficient dose grid [0,0.5,1,2,4,8]; ESMFold→DSSP α-helix; primary = permutation dose-response trend test on the all-generations helix endpoint (TEST, invalid→0), BH-FDR; matched-control + same-norm sham for specificity; secondary SAE-clamp (L26) = negative

main_experiment.key_stats: site-28 CAA dose-response ρ=0.922, p=5.0e-5, BH-FDR q=1.5e-4; winning coef 1.0 helix 0.482 vs baseline 0.414 (+0.068, 95% CI [+0.040,+0.098]), Cliff's δ=0.135, Hedges g=0.237; up to +0.161 at coef 4; matched-control −0.024 (n.s.) & sham −0.005 (n.s.) → CAA exceeds both (+0.093 p=9e-10; +0.073 p=1e-6); survives length-matching (+0.089 in [40,90]); no aa-composition bias
main_experiment.headline: CAA steering along a site-28 residual direction produces a specific, dose-dependent increase in the α-helical content of Evo2-7B's DNA-encoded proteins.

iteration.final_reviewer_status: PASS held (reviewer consistency check clean — dose ladder, ρ/q, winning gain+CI, specificity, length-matched gain, and model-swap robustness all reconcile with no numeric drift)

claims.final_status: ✓ holds — supported, robust (model-swap reproduces), reviewer PASS (round score 7/10 'almost'); no back-edge needed
caveats: Off-target: winning setting shortens protein length (−36.6 aa, Cliff's δ −0.45) and lowers GC (−0.139) — CAA-specific, documented; C1 survives length-matching and shows no composition bias.
Per-generation effect size is small (δ=0.135) though the CI excludes 0 and the trend q=1.5e-4.
SAE-clamp secondary arm negative (helix decreases with clamp; SAE recon_rel_error≈1.0).

figures.caption: α-helix fraction (all generations, invalid→0) vs steering coefficient for CAA at site 28 (primary), site 30, and the SAE-clamp arm; baseline ≈0.414. Site-28 CAA rises monotonically; site 30 peaks at coef 2 then collapses; the SAE arm declines.

Direction-specificity at the winning setting (site 28, coef 1.0): α-helix fraction for baseline, CAA, matched-control, and same-norm sham. CAA raises helix (+0.068 vs baseline) while both controls show no gain.

claims.statement: At the C1-winning intervention setting, Evo2-7B's generated DNA sequences remain valid (well-formed / biologically plausible ORFs) at a rate non-inferior to baseline (pre-registered margin −0.05). Validity is preserved within the margin, but not all other sequence properties are: the intervention substantially shifts GC content (−0.139) and inferred protein length (−37%), which are documented, CAA-specific off-target effects.
